title: Lecture 16 · Transcription, RNA processing and translation

blocks.html:
What to know

  • Transcription copies DNA into RNA. RNA polymerase reads the template strand and builds an RNA strand complementary to it.
  • RNA is processed before export. A 5′ cap and 3′ poly(A) tail protect the transcript; splicing removes introns and joins exons.
  • Translation reads codons. Ribosomes match each three-base codon to a transfer RNA carrying an amino acid; the genetic code is redundant but not ambiguous.
  • Post-translational modification changes function. Phosphorylation, glycosylation, cleavage, and disulfide formation can activate, target, or degrade a protein.
  • Gene expression is regulated at many levels. Transcription factors, chromatin state, RNA stability, and translation rate all change how much protein a cell makes.

Check

check.question: What is removed from a pre-mRNA during splicing?
check.explanation: Splicing removes introns and joins exons. The cap and tail are added and retained to protect and export the mature mRNA.
